title: Precious Stones and Precious Metals (Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing) Bill
what_it_is: Precious Stones and Precious Metals (Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing) Bill

sections.label: Cash transaction reporting regime introduced
sections.summary: In 2014 the CDSA cash transaction reporting regime was introduced, requiring PSMD to perform customer due diligence, keep records and file reports for cash transactions over S$20,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In 2014, the cash transaction reporting regime under the Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes Act (CDSA) was introduced.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This requires PSMD to perform customer due diligence, keep records and file cash transaction reports for cash transactions exceeding S$20,000.

sections.label: Bill strengthens PSMD supervisory regime
sections.summary: The Bill establishes a risk-focused supervisory and regulatory regime addressing ML/TF risks in the PSMD sector, regulating regulated dealing and intermediary businesses and adding measures beyond cash transaction reporting.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Bill will strengthen existing measures by establishing a comprehensive supervisory and regulatory regime that is risk-focused and which addresses the specific ML/TF risks in the PSMD sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: It will allow us to prevent dealing in precious stones and precious metals from being used to facilitate ML/TF by, firstly, regulating persons who carry on a business of regulated dealing or business as an intermediary for regulated dealing; and secondly, providing for additional measures beyond the current cash transaction reporting regime for the PSMD sector.

sections.label: Transaction-based requirements for regulated dealers
sections.summary: Transaction-based requirements largely mirror the existing cash transaction reporting regime, including clause 16 requiring regulated dealers to perform customer due diligence in prescribed circumstances and for cash transactions above $20,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The transaction-based requirements are largely similar to existing requirements under the cash transaction reporting regime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: These include clause 16 which requires regulated dealers to perform customer due diligence (CDD) measures under prescribed circumstances, in addition to the existing requirement to do so for cash transactions above $20,000.

sections.label: Entity-based requirements under clause 19
sections.summary: The Bill sets out new entity-based requirements under clause 19, requiring regulated dealers to implement adequate programmes and measures to prevent ML/TF, such as internal policies, procedures and controls.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Bill sets out entity-based requirements, and these are new and provided for under clause 19, which requires regulated dealers to implement adequate programmes and measures to prevent ML/TF, such as the introduction of internal policies, procedures and controls.

sections.label: Penalties for non-compliance
sections.summary: Upon conviction, non-compliance with the Bill may lead to fines not exceeding $100,000 and imprisonment of up to three years, depending on the contravention's nature and severity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Upon conviction, non-compliance with the Bill may lead to fines not exceeding $100,000 and imprisonment terms of up to three years, depending on the nature and severity of the particular contravention.

sections.label: Bill regulates precious stones and metals dealers
sections.summary: Because precious stones and precious minerals are especially susceptible to ML/TF, the Bill seeks to regulate PSMDs to increase AML/CTF measures in the industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These characteristics make precious stones and precious minerals especially susceptible to be used for ML/TF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, in order to increase AML/CTF measures in this industry, this Bill seeks to regulate PSMDs.

sections.label: Overseas persons as regulated dealers
sections.summary: Clause 6 requires a person to be a registered dealer before acting as a regulated dealer, and the question asks whether this applies to overseas-based persons dealing with Singapore individuals or dealers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Thirdly, clause 6 says that "a person must not act or hold out to act as a regulated dealer unless the person is a registered dealer." Would this Bill apply to persons or businesses who are based overseas but who engage in regulated dealing with individuals or dealers in Singapore?

sections.label: Adjusting guidelines for ML/TF risks
sections.summary: Because ML/TF risk profiles change, the Bill allows guidelines, standards and codes of practice to be adjusted under clause 35.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As risk profiles may change due to the dynamic nature of ML/TF, there needs to be a two-way feedback on what works, what does not, how things need to be changed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: That is why it is good that the Bill allows for adjustment of guidelines, standards and codes of practice under clause 35.

sections.label: Industry feedback on customer questions
sections.summary: Industry feedback raised whether questions asked of potential customers are overly intrusive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Indeed, this is part of the feedback that has come from the industry, that is, whether or not the questions to be asked of potential customers are overly intrusive.

sections.label: Disclosure to foreign authorities
sections.summary: Clause 29 provides for disclosure of information or documents to a foreign authority, which supports international cooperation in identifying riskier transactions and limiting use of precious metals and stones in ML/TF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Regarding the information gathered, clause 29 of the Bill provides for disclosure of information or documents to a foreign authority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is good because international cooperation in this area is vital to effectively identify which transactions are riskier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It seeks to limit the use of precious metals and precious stones in ML/TF.

sections.label: PSMD sector AML risk area
sections.summary: The Financial Action Task Force in 2016 identified the PSMD sector as a risk area for improved controls, and it is not currently subject to specific AML/CTF controls in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Financial Action Task Force, in its evaluation of Singapore's AML framework in 2016, has identified the PSMD sector as a risk area for controls to be improved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The PSMD sector in Singapore is not currently subject to any specific AML/CTF controls.

sections.label: Errant lawyer jewellery trust case
sections.summary: In 2006 an errant lawyer used about $2 million held on trust to buy jewellery and precious stones from a jeweller and absconded with the items.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The case of an errant lawyer in 2006 is a good example.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: He had used approximately $2 million that he held on trust for his client to purchase various pieces of jewellery and precious stones from a jeweller and absconded with all these items.

sections.label: Splitting purchases below threshold
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry would address purchasers spreading purchases across PSMDs below the $20,000 threshold to avoid CDD requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This has a salutary effect of ensuring common standards as well as ensuring that compliance costs are kept in check.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I wonder how the Ministry would deal with possible situations arising where purchasers could spread their purchases with PSMDs to escape detection by transacting below the threshold amount of $20,000 so as to escape CDD requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: What expectations will be placed on PSMDs to find out whether such multiple purchases were or will be made?

sections.label: Definition of business and period
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the period is five years as for pawnbrokers and defines 'business' from the Business Names Registration Act (2014).

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Would this be, for example, five years, as in the case for pawnbrokers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked what the definition of "business" is in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We would draw from the Business Names Registration Act (2014) and I would just like to define it as such: "'Business' would include every form of trade, commerce and profession and any other activity that is carried on for the purposes of gain but does not include any office, employment or occupation".

sections.label: Part III applies to regulated dealers
sections.summary: Clause 14 of the Bill states that Part III requirements apply to all regulated dealers carrying on regulated dealing in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As stated in clause 14 of the Bill, the requirements of Part III, which deals with this aspect of Mr de Souza's concern, apply to all regulated dealers who carry on any part of their business of regulated dealing in Singapore.

sections.label: CDD for two daily transactions
sections.summary: Under clause 15, regulated dealers must perform CDD measures if two or more transactions in a single day exceed the $20,000 threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As Mr Murali Pillai knows, under clause 15, the regulated dealers are required to perform CDD measures on a customer if there are two or more transactions in a single day which exceed the threshold of $20,000.

sections.label: Five-year record-keeping period
sections.summary: The Ministry intends to prescribe in subsidiary legislation that dealers keep records for a period of five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On the record-keeping requirement, Mr Murali Pillai asked about the prescribed period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We do intend to prescribe in the subsidiary legislation for dealers to keep records for a period of five years.

sections.label: Power to prescribe different periods
sections.summary: The Ministry does not intend to prescribe different time periods now but wants power to adjust record-keeping requirements later if needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: At this point in time, we do not intend to prescribe different time periods but would like to have the power to do so and make the adjustments at a later stage if we assess that there is a need to impose more stringent record-keeping requirements on certain prescribed classes of dealers or transactions.

sections.label: AML/CTF standards in PSMD sector
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens AML/CTF standards in the PSMD sector through supervision and regulation to manage ML/TF risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In line with the broader AML/CTF framework, this Bill will strengthen AML/CTF standards in the PSMD sector through supervision and regulation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It will help to manage ML/TF risks within the sector, which, as Members have pointed out, is something that has been missing; this is one further piece amongst the various steps that we take.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This would be crucial to combat crime and also improve security both domestically and globally.
